title: Email and Notification Integration
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of email and notification integration in a Classic ASP application.
Identify and describe at least two syllabus subtopics: Email workflow fundamentals and SMTP concepts.
Inspect a minimal example and define a reproducible normal-case and failure-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study email and notification integration as part of Classic ASP development and legacy maintenance. The lesson follows the attached ASP curriculum topic 82 and uses the syllabus subtopics as the coverage checklist.
content.why_it_matters: Email and Notification Integration matters because Classic ASP behavior crosses a server-side scripting engine, IIS configuration, request/response boundaries, and often COM or ADO dependencies. A small, explicit test helps distinguish intended behavior from runtime-specific behavior.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Classic ASP often relies on Windows COM components and external services for file operations, messaging, XML, and integration. For 'Email and Notification Integration', document the exact component/provider version, permissions, bitness, network boundaries, timeouts, and recovery behavior. Never construct a filesystem path or external URL directly from untrusted input, and keep secrets outside the public web root and repository.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus coverage
content_blocks.text: The lesson explicitly covers: Email workflow fundamentals; SMTP concepts; Reviewing legacy email components; Sending notifications from server-side code; Handling provider and delivery failures; Protecting credentials; Avoiding mail-header injection. Treat these subtopics as connected requirements. For each one, be able to define the concept, identify where it appears in a Classic ASP application, and name one test or diagnostic that would verify it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Email and Notification Integration
content_blocks.code:
<%
' Illustration only: CDO/provider-specific delivery settings are required.
Dim mail
Set mail = Server.CreateObject("CDO.Message")
mail.Subject = "Test notification"
mail.TextBody = "Synthetic test message"
' Set From/To and restricted SMTP configuration before Send.
' mail.Send
Set mail = Nothing
%>
content_blocks.expected_output: The message object is prepared, but no email is sent by this safe starter.

content_blocks.text: Use approved test data and a component/service you control. Confirm path permissions, host allow-lists, timeouts, malformed responses, and cleanup behavior. content_blocks.title: Guided workflow
content_blocks.text: 1. Start with a minimal local example of email and notification integration. 2. Trace its inputs, state changes, dependencies, and output. 3. Test a normal case, a missing/malformed case, and one permission/provider/runtime failure. 4. Write down the exact expected and observed result before changing another variable.

content_blocks.text: Create a small, reviewable demonstration of email and notification integration using synthetic data. Include at least one of these syllabus concepts: Email workflow fundamentals. common_mistakes.problem: Treating legacy runtime behavior as universal.
common_mistakes.why: IIS versions, Windows lifecycle, COM registration/bitness, and ADO providers can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down the actual server/provider versions and validate on a disposable test site.

common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing records, expired sessions, permissions, timeouts, and malformed data reveal different failure modes.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, negative, and boundary cases with expected outcomes.

common_mistakes.why: Detailed errors can reveal paths, SQL text, configuration, and component information.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep diagnostics in restricted server-side logs and return a generic message with a reference ID.
